label: Cosmology
summary: NASA describes cosmology as the way we conceptualize and study the universe, concerned with its origin, evolution and nature.

sources.title: OECD Frascati Manual 2015 — Fields of R&D classification
Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/the-big-bang/

label: Standard Model of particle physics
summary: CERN describes the Standard Model of particle physics as a framework relating fundamental particles to the electromagnetic, strong and weak forces and their carrier particles; gravity is not included.

sources.title: The Standard Model
Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

label: Black holes

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/black-holes/

summary: NASA describes black holes as extremely dense concentrations of matter with an event horizon, a boundary from beneath which nothing, including light, can escape.

label: Higgs mechanism

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/higgs-boson/

summary: CERN describes the Brout–Englert–Higgs mechanism as the interaction by which elementary particles gain mass through the Higgs field. It states that stronger interaction gives greater mass, while photons do not interact with the field and have no mass.

label: Higgs boson

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/higgs-boson/

summary: CERN describes the Higgs boson as a wave in the Higgs field. It reports that the particle announced by ATLAS and CMS on 4 July 2012 was concluded, after additional data in March 2013, to be some kind of Higgs boson.

label: Quarks

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

summary: CERN describes quarks as one of two basic types of matter particles, with six members arranged in three generations: up and down, charm and strange, top and bottom. It states that quarks have three colour types and combine into colourless objects.

label: Leptons

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

summary: CERN describes six leptons arranged in three generations: electron and electron neutrino, muon and muon neutrino, tau and tau neutrino. The charged electron, muon and tau are distinguished from electrically neutral neutrinos with very small mass.

label: Gluons

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

summary: CERN identifies gluons as boson force carriers responsible for the strong force in the Standard Model.

label: Stellar evolution

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/

summary: NASA describes a star's life cycle as formation from collapsing clouds of gas and dust, a long phase powered by hydrogen fusion, and later changes whose outcomes depend strongly on stellar mass.

label: White dwarfs

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/

summary: In its account of low-mass stellar death, NASA describes a white dwarf as the remaining stellar core after the outer layers are expelled, a roughly Earth-sized remnant that cools over billions of years.

label: Neutron stars

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/

summary: NASA identifies a neutron star as one possible extremely dense surviving core remnant of a high-mass star after a core-collapse supernova.

label: Supernovae

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/

summary: NASA describes a core-collapse supernova of a high-mass star as a huge explosion driven by the collapse and rebound of an iron core, sending a shock wave outward and leaving a dense remnant such as a neutron star or black hole.

label: Accretion disks

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/black-holes/

summary: NASA describes accretion disks around black holes as rings of gas and dust that emit light across many wavelengths, including X-rays.

label: Cosmic microwave background

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/astrophysics/programs/physics-of-the-cosmos/big-bang-and-the-evolution-of-the-universe/

summary: NASA describes the cosmic microwave background as early-universe light decoupled from matter about 380,000 years after the Big Bang and stretched by cosmic expansion to a glow at about 2.7 kelvin.

label: Inflationary cosmology

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/astrophysics/programs/physics-of-the-cosmos/big-bang-and-the-evolution-of-the-universe/

summary: NASA describes the inflation hypothesis as a brief period of extraordinary expansion connected to the formation of large-scale cosmic structure. It identifies CMB observations as a probe and states that the physical process behind inflation remains unknown.

label: Big Bang nucleosynthesis

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/overview/

summary: In its account of cosmic history, NASA describes Big Bang nucleosynthesis as the early period when collisions of protons and neutrons produced hydrogen, helium and traces of lithium and beryllium, before expansion and cooling stopped further element formation.

label: Large-scale structure

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/astrophysics/programs/physics-of-the-cosmos/big-bang-and-the-evolution-of-the-universe/

summary: NASA describes galaxies and galaxy clusters as the large-scale structure associated, in its inflation account, with the growth of small early density fluctuations.

label: Higgs field

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/higgs-boson/

summary: CERN describes the Higgs field as a field proposed in 1964 that fills the universe, with the Higgs boson as a wave in it. In the described mechanism, elementary particles that interact with the field acquire mass; photons do not interact with it and remain massless.

label: Neutrinos

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

summary: CERN describes electron, muon and tau neutrinos as the electrically neutral members of the lepton generations, with very small mass.

label: Gluon

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

summary: CERN identifies the gluon as boson force carriers responsible for the strong force in the Standard Model.

label: Photon

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

summary: CERN identifies the photon as boson force carriers responsible for the electromagnetic force in the Standard Model.

label: W and Z bosons

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

summary: CERN identifies the W and Z bosons as boson force carriers responsible for the weak force in the Standard Model.

label: Higgs boson discovery

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/higgs-boson/

summary: CERN reports that ATLAS and CMS announced a new particle on 4 July 2012. Its lack of electric charge, short lifetime and decay patterns matched Higgs expectations; examination of additional data led to the conclusion in March 2013 that some kind of Higgs boson had been discovered.

label: Big Bang cosmology

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/overview/

summary: NASA's account of cosmologists' theories describes the Big Bang as the transfer of inflation-driving energy to matter and light, followed by an extremely hot early universe that expanded and cooled through nucleosynthesis and recombination.

label: Cosmic inflation

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/astrophysics/programs/physics-of-the-cosmos/big-bang-and-the-evolution-of-the-universe/

summary: NASA describes inflation as a brief period of extraordinary cosmic expansion in which small density fluctuations ultimately led to galaxies and galaxy clusters. It states that CMB-map properties are consistent with inflation predictions while the physical process driving inflation remains unknown.

label: Primordial nucleosynthesis

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/overview/

summary: In its account of cosmic history, NASA describes primordial nucleosynthesis as the early period when protons and neutrons produced hydrogen, helium and traces of lithium and beryllium as the expanding universe cooled.

label: LZ high-energy recoil-like event
summary: LZ reports one event consistent with a nuclear recoil at 248 ± 23 (statistical) ± 23 (systematic) keV in a 2.84 tonne-year xenon exposure. Its profile-likelihood test gives 2.6 sigma global tension with a background-only hypothesis after look-elsewhere effects, compared with a maximum local significance of 3.4 sigma across the tested models; this is a reported event of interest, not a dark-matter discovery.

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://lz.lbl.gov/

label: Look-elsewhere corrected significance
summary: LZ illustrates the distinction between local and look-elsewhere-corrected global significance: for its reported xenon recoil event, the maximum local significance across tested models is 3.4 sigma, while the global significance after look-elsewhere effects is 2.6 sigma relative to a background-only hypothesis.
